title: Making the Zeros True: Fitting the Joint Offsets of a Leg From Where the Foot Was Measured, and What It Cannot Fix

questions.question: Where does a joint offset come from?
options: The servo's gears wear, and the zero moves with them
The link lengths differ a little from the drawing
The servo's zero is wherever the horn was pressed on the shaft
The foot's place is measured with noise
questions.explanation: The horn goes on the spline one tooth one way or the other, so the servo's zero is a few degrees from the model's. It is a fixed error for each joint.

questions.question: The foot was how far from where it was commanded before the fit?
options: 3.4 mm
2 mm, the noise of one axis
35 mm
questions.explanation: Offsets of 2, -3 and 4 degrees moved the foot 14.6 mm on average. After the fit 3.4 mm was left.

questions.question: What was left after the fit?
options: An offset in the knee, which cannot be fitted
The noise of the measurements
Nothing: the foot was at the commanded place
The error of the link lengths
questions.explanation: Noise of 2 mm in each of three axes is 3.5 mm in all, and 3.4 mm is what remained. The fit removed everything it could.

questions.question: Why does a leg straight in every pose give no fit?
options: The leg cannot be measured accurately at full stretch
The knee's offset cannot be told from the hip's
A straight leg is out of the jig's range
The lean's offset has no effect on a straight leg
questions.explanation: With the leg straight a little more knee and a little less hip move the foot the same way, so the equations are singular. The function says false.

questions.question: What does a large residual after the fit say?
options: More poses are needed
The measurements were taken in the wrong order
The model, not only the zeros, is wrong (for example a link length)
The offsets found are larger than a spline tooth
questions.explanation: With a thigh 10 mm longer than the model says the fit ran and left 3.6 mm that no offsets could explain. Fit or measure the lengths; do not accept the calibration.

questions.question: Why use a dozen poses and not one?
options: Noise has nothing to average against with one
One pose gives three numbers, too few for three offsets
The fit only converges with ten poses or more
To check that the servos repeat
questions.explanation: One bent pose gives three coordinates for three unknowns, so it has an answer, but the answer carries all the noise of that one measurement.
